content.text:
Interesting: Rust MENU_LABELS is a global static shared by all windows; set_menu_labels refreshes all menus. So each window's locale sync writes global labels; last window to change wins. On reload, one window writes labels for its locale; other windows inherit that language in the native menu even if their UI is another language. That's actually an existing multi-window issue. The removal of broadcast means: if window A changes locale, window B's native menu (global MENU_LABELS) will be refreshed to A's locale because `set_menu_labels` calls `refresh_all_menus`, while B's web UI stays old. Previously reload of A also changed menu globally, B stayed old. So not a regression in that regard; but maybe "broadcast between windows" intent was to make B also reload. Need evidence.

Let's inspect rust refresh_menu to see menu creation uses global labels. Also check whether ls labels only translated, untranslated fallback English means switching to English with empty map resets to English because overwrite Some(empty). Yes `set_menu_labels` sets Some(labels), so empty map falls back to English. So native menu switching to English works. But there is global shared state across windows: changing in one changes menu for all windows. On the old reload, same. No regression.

Need inspect Monaco 0.52.2 MenuRegistry to validate applyMonacoLocale mechanism and identify stale surfaces. Read actions.js. Also inspect `MenuRegistry.appendMenuItem` and `_menuItems` values type. Need see if direct mutation triggers menu update. Let's read.

## 3. `addAction` e as ações do Calcpad

`addAction` retorna `DisposableStore` (ou `Disposable.None` se não houver keybinding service). O dispose remove comando, item de menu, keybindings e a action interna (`standaloneCodeEditor.js:112-143`). O item de menu tem `when` com `editorId` do editor atual (`standaloneCodeEditor.js:104`, `124-128`), então ao recriar o editor ele não aparece no novo — mas continua no registry global.

No Calcpad:

- As 4 ações de `main.ts:1206-1223`, `1226-1232`, `1236-1242`, `1247-1300` ignoram o retorno.

## 4. Dispose/recreate dos editores com os mesmos models

Os models sobrevivem: o `TabManager` cria models separados (`tab-manager.ts:496-497`), anexa via `setModel` (`341`, `375`) e usa refcount (`525-530`). O editor criado com `value` cria um model próprio e o descarta no primeiro detach (`standaloneCodeEditor.js:186-201`, `224-230`); models do TabManager não são owned. `options.model` é suportado (`editor.api.d.ts:1373`).

Mas `TabManager` e `EditorGroup` guardam o editor fixo (`tab-manager.ts:93-96`; `editor-group.ts:13`, `21-24`), então trocar o editor exige refatorar ambos e refazer toda a fiação (listeners, diagnostics, comandos). ## 5. Recarregar só os módulos/chunks do Monaco?

Não há caminho suportado.

- No build de produção, o núcleo do Monaco está no **mesmo chunk do app**: `dist/assets/index-*.js` tem ~6,1 MB e contém Monaco; só as grammars de linguagens viram chunks separados. O `vite.config.ts` não define `manualChunks`; as opções de build são só `outDir` e comentários legais (`vite.config.ts:182-192`).
- `import * as monaco from 'monaco-editor'` é estático e resolve para esse chunk. ES modules não podem ser “descarregados”.
- `import(/* @vite-ignore */ url + '?v=2')` só funcionaria com um asset separado; ainda assim criaria uma **segunda instância** do módulo, com `StandaloneServices`, `CommandsRegistry`, `EditorExtensionsRegistry`, model service e workers próprios (`workers.ts:3-10` é global). Models/editor da instância antiga não cruzam para a nova.
- Reexecutar o chunk principal reexecuta `bootstrap()`/`createApp()` (`main.ts:240+`), ou seja, duplica o app.
- A única forma de “recarregar só o Monaco” preservando o app é um **iframe** com um bundle Monaco-only: o parent mantém o estado e recria o iframe; documentos precisam ser serializados por `postMessage`. Models, undo stack, markers e providers teriam de ser reconstruídos. É a solução completa sem reload da página, mas não é pequena.

## Veredito

Não há troca de idioma do Monaco em runtime suportada neste setup. A maior parte dos rótulos nativos é materializada na importação dos módulos; o locale do plugin é memoizado; e não existe API para atualizar labels já registrados. Recriar editores com os mesmos models refresca apenas uma minoria. A troca completa exige recarregar o documento/webview — ou isolar o Monaco num iframe recarregável.

## 1. O que é resolvido quando

**Na importação/registro (fica congelado):**

- `monaco-editor/esm/vs/editor/editor.main.js:1-7` importa `edcore.main.js`, que importa `editor.all.js` (`edcore.main.js:5-14`); `editor.all.js:5+` importa todos os contributions. Cada contribution chama `registerEditorAction(...)` no topo do módulo: 168 ocorrências em 42 arquivos. `registerEditorAction` instancia a action e a registra (`editorExtensions.js:316-320`), e `Command.register()` grava comando e item de menu (`editorExtensions.js:21-80`).
- Exemplos de labels congelados no import: Find/Replace (`findController.js:423-440`, `572-620`, `790-809`, registro em `843-849`), Cut/Copy/Paste e submenus (`clipboard.js:39-99`, `136-146`, `238`), Format Document/Selection (`formatActions.js:188`, `215`, `247-248`), “Show Editor Context Menu” (`contextmenu.js:328`), Suggest (`suggestController.js:659`, `922`).
- Menus de contexto/submenus: `MenuRegistry.appendMenuItem` guarda o título no momento do registro (`actions.js:283-295`); `MenuItemAction.label` lê esse título já resolvido (`actions.js:344-356`). Há 19 `appendMenuItem` em 9 arquivos.
- Find widget: constantes de módulo em `findWidget.js:37-51`, usadas na construção do widget em `746-997`.
- Suggest widget: mensagens estáticas em `suggestWidget.js:80-81`, usadas em `365-381`.
- Strings standalone/aria/command palette: objetos `QuickCommandNLS`, `GoToLineNLS`, `StandaloneCodeEditorNLS` etc. em `standaloneStrings.js:11-44`; uso em `standaloneCommandsQuickAccess.js:57-79` e `standaloneCodeEditor.js:68`.

**Lazy (resolvido na criação/chamada do widget):**

- Detalhes de itens do Suggest (`suggestWidget.js:168-189`), “Show More/Less” (`suggestController.js:857-863`).
- Hover e parameter hints (`markdownHoverParticipant.js:85-111`, `368-375`; `parameterHintsWidget.js:214`).
- Contagem/validação do Find (`findWidget.js:317-342`; `findController.js:640-688`).
- Aviso de limite de multicursores e ação “Increase Multi Cursor Limit” (`codeEditorWidget.js:1214-1223`).
- Separadores do command palette (`commandsQuickAccess.js:150-205`).

Porém **todas** passam por `__calcpadTr`, e `__calcpadLocale()` devolve `__calcpadResolved` memoizado (`vite.config.ts:71`, `86-102`). Como o import do Monaco já dispara vários `localize` de topo, o locale é congelado no startup. Não há export para resetar esse cache (`vite.config.ts:103-106`).

Além disso, o plugin só transforma `localize('key', 'English')` com key string literal e presente nos mapas (`vite.config.ts:112-113`, `136`). Chamadas com objeto `localize({ key: ... })` — 62 ocorrências em `vs/editor` — permanecem em inglês mesmo após reload.

## 2. Existe API para atualizar labels já registrados?

Não.

- `IEditorAction.label` é `readonly` (`editor.api.d.ts:2540-2547`), e `addAction` apenas adiciona, retornando `IDisposable` (`editor.api.d.ts:1434`; `standaloneCodeEditor.js:93-144`).
- `MenuRegistry` só tem `addCommand`, `appendMenuItem`, `getMenuItems`; não há update/remove de título (`actions.js:257-333`).
- `EditorContributionRegistry` só registra e lê actions/contributions; não há unregister (`editorExtensions.js:362-393`).
- `registerEditorAction` não guarda disposable e não remove nada (`editorExtensions.js:316-320`).
- `monaco.editor.addEditorAction` também só adiciona (`standaloneEditor.js:105-146`; `editor.api.d.ts:1009`).
- `CommandsRegistry.registerCommand` devolve disposable para remover o handler, mas não atualiza metadata/menu (`commands.js:18-58`).

Hack interno (importar `vs/editor/browser/editorExtensions.js` e `vs/platform/actions/common/actions.js`, mutar `.label` e títulos) é possível em parte, mas não cobre Find widget, mensagens estáticas do Suggest nem NLS de standalone; é não suportado e não resolve o problema.

## 3. `addAction` e as ações do Calcpad

`addAction` retorna `DisposableStore` (ou `Disposable.None` se não houver keybinding service). O dispose remove comando, item de menu, keybindings e a action interna (`standaloneCodeEditor.js:112-143`). O item de menu tem `when` com `editorId` do editor atual (`standaloneCodeEditor.js:104`, `124-128`), então ao recriar o editor ele não aparece no novo — mas continua no registry global.

No Calcpad:

- As 4 ações de `main.ts:1206-1223`, `1226-1232`, `1236-1242`, `1247-1300` ignoram o retorno.
- `formatting-commands.ts:34-40` coleta os disposables e devolve um agregado em `64`, mas `main.ts:1190` descarta o retorno.
- `group.disposables` existe e é disposto antes do editor (`editor-group.ts:19`, `27-34`), mas não recebe esses disposables.

Pior: `editor.addCommand` (Alt+Z e Ctrl+D em `main.ts:1182-1185`) retorna apenas `commandId`, não disposable (`standaloneCodeEditor.js:80-89`). Recriar editores duplicaria/ deixaria handlers dinâmicos globais apontando para editores mortos. Isso é um bloqueio real para “dispose + recreates” sem refatorar a fiação.

## 4. Dispose/recreate dos editores com os mesmos models

Os models sobrevivem: o `TabManager` cria models separados (`tab-manager.ts:496-497`), anexa via `setModel` (`341`, `375`) e usa refcount (`525-530`). O editor criado com `value` cria um model próprio e o descarta no primeiro detach (`standaloneCodeEditor.js:186-201`, `224-230`); models do TabManager não são owned. `options.model` é suportado (`editor.api.d.ts:1373`).

Mas `TabManager` e `EditorGroup` guardam o editor fixo (`tab-manager.ts:93-96`; `editor-group.ts:13`, `21-24`), então trocar o editor exige refatorar ambos e refazer toda a fiação (listeners, diagnostics, comandos). O handle de diagnostics nem é guardado/disposto (`main.ts:1193`; `diagnostics.ts:57-63`).

| Rótulo | Resolvido em | Atualiza com recreate? |
|---|---|---|
| Ações nativas (Find, Format, Cut, etc.) | import | **Não**: labels copiados das ações globais para o novo editor (`codeEditorWidget.js:201-212`) |
| Itens de menu/contexto/submenus | import | **Não**: título armazenado no `MenuRegistry` |
| Find widget (labels, placeholders, aria) | import | **Não**: constantes de módulo (`findWidget.js:37-51`) |
| Suggest “Loading...” / “No suggestions.” | import | **Não**: fields estáticos (`suggestWidget.js:80-81`) |
| Command Palette / Go to Line / aria standalone | import | **Não**: `standaloneStrings.js:11-44` |
| Ações `calcpad.*` via `addAction` | na chamada de `addAction` | **Sim**, se dispose + re-add com os labels novos |
| Detalhes de Suggest, hover, contagem/validação do Find, aviso de multicursor | lazy | **Sim, em tese**, mas só se `__calcpadResolved` for invalidado e o widget for recriado |
| Comandos de formatação Calcpad | hardcoded | **Não**: labels fixos em inglês (`formatting-commands.ts:43-62`) |

Em resumo: recriar editores sem mexer no cache e nos registros globais não muda quase nada; mesmo com o cache corrigido, a maior parte dos rótulos visíveis continua no idioma antigo.

## 5. Recarregar só os módulos/chunks do Monaco?

Não há caminho suportado.

- No build de produção, o núcleo do Monaco está no **mesmo chunk do app**: `dist/assets/index-*.js` tem ~6,1 MB e contém Monaco; só as grammars de linguagens viram chunks separados. O `vite.config.ts` não define `manualChunks`; as opções de build são só `outDir` e comentários legais (`vite.config.ts:182-192`).
- `import * as monaco from 'monaco-editor'` é estático e resolve para esse chunk. ES modules não podem ser “descarregados”.
- `import(/* @vite-ignore */ url + '?v=2')` só funcionaria com um asset separado; ainda assim criaria uma **segunda instância** do módulo, com `StandaloneServices`, `CommandsRegistry`, `EditorExtensionsRegistry`, model service e workers próprios (`workers.ts:3-10` é global). Models/editor da instância antiga não cruzam para a nova.
- Reexecutar o chunk principal reexecuta `bootstrap()`/`createApp()` (`main.ts:240+`), ou seja, duplica o app.
- A única forma de “recarregar só o Monaco” preservando o app é um **iframe** com um bundle Monaco-only: o parent mantém o estado e recria o iframe; documentos precisam ser serializados por `postMessage`. Models, undo stack, markers e providers teriam de ser reconstruídos. É a solução completa sem reload da página, mas não é pequena.

## 6. Menor abordagem viável

**Recomendação: manter reload completo, mas torná-lo lossless e implementá-lo também no web.** É a menor mudança que atualiza o máximo de strings do Monaco — todas as que o plugin transformou.

Situação atual:

- Só o desktop recarrega: o listener está dentro do bloco `if (isTauri && tauriBridge)` (`main.ts:2433`, `2677-2700`). No web, a UI Vue muda ao vivo, mas o Monaco fica no idioma inicial.
- O reload atual salva drafts (`main.ts:2469-2516`, `2686-2690`) e captura só `openFiles`/`activeFile` (`2667-2675`). `WorkspaceStateStore` também só guarda caminhos (`workspace-state.ts:23-29`, `26`).
- Os drafts recuperam conteúdo, mas com prompt e apenas no grupo ativo (`main.ts:2547-2567`, `2569-2595`). Split, ordem das abas, view state e ids dos tabs não são preservados.
- O menu nativo já atualiza ao vivo via `watch(localeRef, syncMenu)` (`main.ts:335-343`); só o Monaco força reload.

Menor implementação:

1. Mover o listener de `LOCALE_CHANGED_EVENT` para fora do bloco Tauri, valendo também no web.
2. Antes do reload, serializar por aba: grupo/ordem, id, título, path, dirty, conteúdo, viewState e aba/grupo ativo — `sessionStorage`/IndexedDB no web, store temporário no desktop.
3. Gravar um flag de “reload por locale” e, no boot, restaurar o snapshot silenciosamente, sem o prompt de drafts.
4. Garantir que `localStorage['calcpad.locale']` contenha o locale resolvido antes do reload. Cuidado com `auto`: o módulo virtual lê `window.__CALCPAD_CURRENT_CULTURE__`/`__CALCPAD_HOST_LOCALE__` (`vite.config.ts:91-93`), mas só o webview do VS Code define esses globais (`calcpadVueUIProvider.ts:1068`). No desktop, grave o tag resolvido ou exponha o culture antes do import.
5. Aceitar que strings com `localize({ key: ... })` e keys fora dos mapas continuam em inglês mesmo após reload (`vite.config.ts:112-113`, `136`).

O que ficaria stale sem reload total (mesmo com cache reset + recreate + re-add das ações Calcpad): labels de todas as ações nativas, itens de menu/contexto/submenus, Find widget, “Loading...”/“No suggestions.” do Suggest, strings de quick access/Go to Line/aria standalone. Ou seja, a maior parte da UI nativa do Monaco ficaria num idioma misturado.

Se “live” significar obrigatoriamente não recarregar a página: a única opção completa é o iframe Monaco. Recriar editores in-place é um meio-termo que não recomendo: exige refatorar `TabManager`/`EditorGroup`, tratar o vazamento de `addCommand`, re-registrar diagnostics e ainda entrega resultado incompleto.

## 7. VS Code webview

É um caso diferente e não sofre do problema do Monaco:

- Não há import de `monaco` em `vscode-calcpad/src` (grep sem ocorrências). O painel Vue é só Vue; o editor de fato é o editor nativo do VS Code.

- Se o VS Code recarregar o webview, o locale é reinjetado; se apenas o usuário troca o idioma no app, a UI Vue muda ao vivo. O idioma do chrome do VS Code é controlado pelo próprio VS Code (reload de janela dele), não pelo app.

## Ranking final

1. **Menor e completa**: reload completo + snapshot de abas/buffers; já existe no desktop, falta no web e falta preservar split/ordem/view state.
2. **Sem reload de página**: iframe Monaco recarregável; completa, mas refatoração grande.

It translates based on reverse map of current *translated* strings. Potential issue: after first switch to pt-BR, command.title becomes pt text. On second switch to zh, `retranslate` calls `__calcpadTranslate(ptText, 'zh')`. The reverse index includes translations from all maps keyed by translated text, so it can map pt text back to id and then zh text. It builds `__calcpadReverse` once from all maps, including English? It adds values from all maps, and English-to-id entries are added lazily by `__calcpadTr` as modules are loaded. For a command title originally English, it maps via `__calcpadEnglishIndex`. Good. But if a translated string is ambiguous (same text maps to multiple ids), `__calcpadTranslate` returns undefined unless all values agree; then it leaves the old language. This is a potential intermittent stale label, especially for common words. The prior commit 292e19b7 "Remove the redundant English-to-ID map" maybe altered. Need inspect `292e19b7` to see if English-to-ID map removal affects reverse translation. But current code has `__calcpadEnglishById` (not old English-to-ID map?). Let's inspect commit 292e19b7. It might have removed a separate map but left `__calcpadEnglishById`. Not central.

It won't handle text with mixed dynamic content (e.g., "Line 3, Column 4" or "1 of 5 matches"), but many are lazy and now use `__calcpadTr` after reset for future. `uniqueId = editorId + ':' + id`, so 55b0154e correct for addAction. Good. But there is subtlety: `_actions.set(id, internalAction)` stores by original id; action label is mutated. Menu command title keyed by uniqueId; code updates it. Fine.

Now, current `applyMonacoLocale` loops every command in `_commands` and retranslates all titles. This includes command titles that are `{ value, original }` objects. It translates based on reverse map of current *translated* strings. Potential issue: after first switch to pt-BR, command.title becomes pt text. On second switch to zh, `retranslate` calls `__calcpadTranslate(ptText, 'zh')`. The reverse index includes translations from all maps keyed by translated text, so it can map pt text back to id and then zh text. It builds `__calcpadReverse` once from all maps, including English? It adds values from all maps, and English-to-id entries are added lazily by `__calcpadTr` as modules are loaded. For a command title originally English, it maps via `__calcpadEnglishIndex`. Good. But if a translated string is ambiguous (same text maps to multiple ids), `__calcpadTranslate` returns undefined unless all values agree; then it leaves the old language. This is a potential intermittent stale label, especially for common words. The prior commit 292e19b7 "Remove the redundant English-to-ID map" maybe altered. Need inspect `292e19b7` to see if English-to-ID map removal affects reverse translation. But current code has `__calcpadEnglishById` (not old English-to-ID map?). Let's inspect commit 292e19b7. It might have removed a separate map but left `__calcpadEnglishById`. Not central.

More important: `applyMonacoLocale`'s `translateText` only translates text nodes whose exact text is a known translation. It won't handle text with mixed dynamic content (e.g., "Line 3, Column 4" or "1 of 5 matches"), but many are lazy and now use `__calcpadTr` after reset for future. Existing open find widget with counts won't be retranslated because the text includes dynamic numbers. It may be stale until next update. That's minor.

It excludes hover, parameter hints, peek views, suggest item details, notifications, breadcrumbs, etc. Hover/parameter hints are lazy and will resolve new locale if created after switch; if currently open, they stay stale. Peek views (references) might be open and stale; but user can reopen. Suggest item details (type info) might be user symbols and intentionally excluded.

- Full reload previously guaranteed all module-level and lazy strings in the new locale. Live switch only updates selected surfaces; some are stale until recreated/reopened. That's the key regression relative to reload, but it's the explicitly requested trade-off (no reload).

- 9f2458e7 commit message: Monaco resolves NLS strings and Calcpad editor actions registered once at startup. Live locale switch updated Vue UI but left editor menu in previous language. Emit event and desktop host flush drafts/session before reloading webview.

- Side effects assumed: captureSession, writeDraft for dirty tabs, workspace.flush; reload current window only. It did not preserve split, tab order, cursor/scroll, preview scroll, agent pending state; drafts restored via prompt; workspace only paths. It did not broadcast to other windows; native menu updated globally via Rust `MENU_LABELS` (all windows), but their Vue/Monaco stayed old.
- 70cf4ed3 (on backup branch) had the same reload with `writeDraft(id)` no throwOnError? Wait 70cf4ed3's diff says `for (const id of dirty) await writeDraft(id); await workspace.flush(); finally window.location.reload();` while 9f2458e7 had same? Earlier 9f2458e7 full diff showed `for (const id of dirty) await writeDraft(id); await workspace.flush(); } finally { window.location.reload(); }`. In b26f2f7c on current branch, it was improved to `writeDraft(id, true)` and no reload on failure. The 8f43e918 parent version shows that improved version. Good to mention: current branch's reload had a guard added by b26f2f7c to not reload if draft/workspace flush failed, preventing data loss. The removed code preserved that guard. Removing reload also removes the failure path. No data loss now because no reload, but the old guard intent (don't destroy unsaved work) is moot.

Interesting: 55482e37 used `shortcutLabel('Undo', ...)` with English strings and fallback to key. Then 33b56466 changed it to use message IDs. This is a fix because the English-to-ID legacy bridge was removed (34e2daa9) and `t('Undo')` no longer resolves. Good. Current code is okay.

But note `t('catalog.undoCtrlZ')` keys exist in en and zh but maybe not in other locales? Since en fallback always available, they'd show English combined label; 33b56466 improves by composing translated `common.undo` + shortcut for locales that have common.undo but not catalog.undoCtrlZ. Good. No regression.

Now question 4: Does preview menu change alter production or non-dev behavior? No: App.vue works identically in web/desktop production; it only changes how label is computed, using existing i18n catalogs. It does change fallback behavior (if a locale lacks `common.undo`, it shows raw key rather than English "Undo"; but vue-i18n fallback to English means common.undo exists in en, so no issue). It also changes text from "Undo (Ctrl+Z)" to "Undo (Ctrl+Z)" same. For languages with translated common.*, composes. No build/production difference.

Vite prebundle changes: only `optimizeDeps` (dev). Production `build` uses plugins `[monacoLanguagePacks(), vue()]`; b07de4a2 added `monacoPrebundle` only inside `optimizeDeps.rolldownOptions`, not in top-level plugins. So no production bundle change. However, `05ec0ce7` temporarily removed `'monaco-editor'` from `optimizeDeps.include` and added exclude; b07de4a2 reverted that and added the prebundle plugin. Net production unchanged. Need verify whether Vite 8 optimizeDeps with rolldownOptions plugins works; it's a dev-only config. Potential risk: duplication of virtual module resolution; `monacoPrebundle` doesn't have `enforce: 'pre'`, but within optimizer plugin order maybe fine. Not a production risk. Could mention not verified by running dev/build (we cannot run builds? Read-only, could run `npm` build? That writes dist, prohibited. We can inspect config only). We can say no production artifact change by code path; not executed build verification.

Now question 5: real regressions/risks vs previous implementation. Need distinguish real regressions from intended changes and pre-existing gaps.

Potential real regressions:
A. Monaco surfaces not covered by live rewrite remain stale until reopened/reloaded. The old reload guaranteed all transformed Monaco strings updated. Examples:
   - Module-level standalone strings (quick input/Go to Line/aria), find widget static constants, suggest "Loading..."/"No suggestions.", context menu labels for built-in actions? The context menu labels are via MenuRegistry, which is rewritten. But command palette? applyMonacoLocale pokes menus to refresh and rewrites command titles. Does it cover command palette labels? `_commands` includes all commands registered by `Command.register` (built-in actions) with `title`? Let's check `Command.register`: `CommandsRegistry.registerCommand({id, handler, metadata})` doesn't store in MenuRegistry._commands. Wait, `MenuRegistry.addCommand` is separate. Built-in editor actions use `registerEditorAction`, which does not add to `MenuRegistry._commands` nor append menu item? Let's inspect `registerEditorAction` / `EditorContributionRegistry.registerEditorAction`: it may register commands and menu items via `Command` class? In `editorExtensions.js` lines 300+ only pushes action into registry. The `EditorAction` constructor likely has `desc` with menus? Let's inspect `EditorAction` class and `registerEditorAction`. Actually built-in editor actions are registered in `EditorExtensionsRegistry` with `desc` and instantiated per editor in `codeEditorWidget`; their labels are resolved at module load. `getSupportedActions()` on editor returns `IEditorAction[]` including built-ins with `label` strings. applyMonacoLocale mutates those labels. Context menu items for built-ins are generated in `contextmenu.js` using `action.label`, so if the action label is mutated, context menu should reflect new label. But `action.label` may be readonly object? It's a string, mutating works. Good.
   - Command palette labels for built-ins: command palette pulls from `MenuRegistry`? In standalone Monaco, command palette gets commands from `ICommandService` or `MenuRegistry`? `standaloneCommandsQuickAccess` uses `CommandsRegistry.getCommands()` and each command's metadata? Let's inspect. If it uses command id, not localized label, maybe raw commands. But likely it uses `MenuRegistry` / `IQuickInputService`. The prior analysis said command palette/quick access strings use `standaloneStrings` and module-level. applyMonacoLocale may not update those. This is a gap.
   - Native find widget: current open widget DOM is translated by `translateUi`, but static placeholders/title/aria? `translateAttributes` translates title/aria-label/placeholder; text nodes translated. But `.find-widget` includes buttons with `aria-label` and `title`; translated if reverse map has those English strings. Likely yes. However find input's current value isn't translated. Fine.
   - Suggest widget static message: included `.suggest-widget .message`, so current open message translated. But there may be `.suggest-widget` other text, e.g. "No suggestions." in a `.message` div; covered. Good.
   - Quick input widget: `.quick-input-widget` current DOM text translated. But quick input strings with dynamic counts may not. Fine.
   - Menu: `.monaco-menu` current open DOM translated. Context menus are reused; translated.
   - Hover/parameter hints/peek views/notifications: not covered. They are lazy; if open at moment of switch, stale until reopened. Some static strings (e.g. "Loading...") in hover may be module-level and stale forever until reload unless DOM translation covers them (not in selector). That's a real gap.
   - Suggest item detail labels: excluded intentionally because could contain user symbols. So some labels stay old.
   - `formatting-commands.ts` labels hardcoded English; not part of NLS, pre-existing. But `applyMonacoLocale` loops CALCPAD_ACTIONS only four; formatting actions remain English. Old reload didn't translate them either because they were hardcoded. Not a regression.
   - Calcpad `saveAsCustomSnippet` action not in CALCPAD_ACTIONS? It is in map? CALCPAD_ACTIONS includes saveAsCustomSnippet. Good.
   - Some Calcpad actions added with `label: (i18n.global as Composer).t(...)`; current updateCalcpadActions uses `translate(messageId)` which uses activeI18n; good.

B. Native menu cross-window inconsistency: The Rust `MENU_LABELS` global updates all windows. When window A switches to French, window B's native menu becomes French while B's Vue/Monaco stays old. Previously reload of A also updated global menu for all windows, same issue. But now with no reload, A's menu and UI update; B's menu changes too but B's UI doesn't. That's a regression introduced by not broadcasting/reloading B? Actually pre-existing from before (reload A changed menu globally). The difference: previously B's UI stayed old too; same. So not new, but if the removed broadcast was intended to sync B, then missing it leaves inconsistency. It is a real risk worth flagging.

C. `set_menu_labels` watch is set up only after i18n creation, before mount. It updates on locale change. Fine. But the `watch(localeRef, syncMenu)` uses default flush (pre? Vue watch default flush 'pre'), so it may run before `applyResolvedLocale` finishes? `composer.locale.value = locale` triggers watch asynchronously (pre-flush on next tick), after active locale set. `syncMenu` calls `menuLabels(t)` with composer `t`, so correct. No issue.

D. The locale event listener is now registered **after** `appInstance` and group setup but before Tauri block. Is there a window where locale can change before listener registration? User can't interact before app mounts; listener registered after mount. Fine. But the event listener is now also active in the **web** build, where there is no Tauri; `applyMonacoLocale` uses virtual NLS; works. In VS Code webview, the listener is not in `CalcpadVuePanel/main.ts` so only announces locale; irrelevant.

E. Critical: `applyMonacoLocale` imports `MenuRegistry` from internal Monaco path. In production, importing this module separately from `monaco-editor` could create a **second instance** if module resolution differs (ESM vs bundled)? Vite resolves both to same module file; likely same singleton. But `monaco-editor` main entry imports `editor.all` etc. The `actions.js` module is shared. In optimized dev prebundle, the app imports `MenuRegistry` from source module while `monaco-editor` import is prebundled into `node_modules/.vite/deps/monaco-editor.js`; the internal `actions.js` may be a separate module instance? This is a real dev-only risk: b07de4a2 prebundles `monaco-editor` into one optimized chunk, and `monaco-locale.ts` imports `monaco-editor/esm/vs/platform/actions/common/actions.js`, which Vite may serve as a separate module (not part of prebundle), creating a second `MenuRegistry` singleton. Then `applyMonacoLocale` would mutate a different registry than the editor uses, so labels wouldn't refresh in dev. Did b07de4a2 address that? It only transforms Monaco prebundle; the internal import may still be separate. In production, both imports are bundled once, so singleton. In dev, Vite's dep optimizer may prebundle `monaco-editor` including actions.js; the internal import from `monaco-locale.ts` is also optimized? Vite optimizeDeps scans imports; it may include the deep import as separate optimized dep or resolve to same prebundled chunk. If not, duplicate. This is a potential dev-only regression from b07de4a2/8f43e918 combo, not production. We cannot verify without running dev server (we could run? Read-only but starting dev server writes cache; not allowed? We must not modify files, and starting Vite writes node_modules/.vite cache. Avoid). We can flag as unverified risk. But the user asked about production behavior; production unaffected.

F. `applyMonacoLocale` uses `MenuRegistry.appendMenuItem(menu, { command: {...} })` for every menu ID including `MenuId.CommandPalette`. `appendMenuItem` creates a `LinkedList` for each. It immediately disposes, which fires `onDidChangeMenu`. It leaves an empty menu entry in `_menuItems` for menu IDs that didn't exist. Not a functional issue. It also adds a fake command id that could show briefly? Disposable immediate. Fine.
G. The fake refresh item has `title: ''`; command id not registered; but menu service builds MenuItemAction and may show blank? It's removed in same microtask; onDidChangeMenu is a MicrotaskEmitter, so events coalesce and menu rebuild sees post-dispose state. Fine.
H. `retranslate` mutates `value.original` too, which may be used to map back? It translates `original` (the original English?) Wait `ILocalizedString` has `value` (translated) and `original` (original English). `retranslate` translates both: if `original` is English, it becomes translated, losing the original for future reverse mapping. That may break subsequent switches back to English or other locales because `original` no longer English. But `value` also translated. The reverse map can map translated strings back to IDs, so maybe okay if unambiguous. But if ambiguous, it may fail. More importantly, `MenuItemAction.label` uses `title.value` (translated). For `LocalizedString` objects, `original` is supposed to remain English. Overwriting it is wrong and could cause loss of fallback. Is this a real regression? It only affects objects in MenuRegistry. If `original` is used by Monaco to detect language or reset, not sure. The current code at 8f43e918 translated both. Could lead to stale labels if translation mapping fails. We can mention as a risk: in-place mutation of `original` means the registry no longer holds the English source, so switching to a language missing that key falls back to the previous translation (because `__calcpadTranslate` returns undefined and code keeps current value) rather than English. Example: switch pt-BR → locale with no translation for that key: `retranslate` gets pt text, reverse maps to id, then `__calcpadMaps[target]?.[module]?.[key] ?? __calcpadEnglishById[id]`. If target lacks key, it uses `__calcpadEnglishById[id]` (English) if the id was seen; so it can return English. If `__calcpadEnglishById` not populated (because __calcpadTr for that module/key never called?), then undefined and it keeps pt. But likely populated on module load. So maybe okay. Still a risk.

I. `applyMonacoLocale` calls `updateCalcpadActions` before retranslating all commands. `updateCalcpadActions` uses `translate(messageId)` from Vue i18n, which returns translated label. Fine. Then generic `retranslateCommand` loops over all commands and may retranslate the Calcpad command titles again using reverse map. If the label is a translated string and reverse maps unambiguously, it stays same. If ambiguous, it may remain. Fine. But ordering could cause double translation attempts; e.g. label "Salvar" (pt for Save) reverse maps to an ID whose zh translation is different; target locale same pt, so returns same. Fine.
J. `updateCalcpadActions` only updates actions for editors that exist at event time. If a new editor group is created after locale change, its `addAction` labels call `translate` at creation (current locale), so fine. If a new editor is created with `editor.getSupportedActions` labels from module-level constants, they'll be in original language? New editor creation after locale switch uses module-level strings already evaluated at startup, but the module-level `localize` calls were transformed to `__calcpadTr` and executed at import time (old locale). So a newly created editor after live switch will have **old-language built-in actions**! Wait, this is crucial. `editor.getSupportedActions()` includes built-in actions instantiated at editor creation from `EditorExtensionsRegistry`? Some action labels are constructed when the editor is created, using `action.label` from registry? Let's inspect `codeEditorWidget.js:201-212` and `EditorAction`/registry. If the editor is created after the locale switch, it copies labels from global action instances that were created at module import (old locale) — so new editors might show old language. The current `applyMonacoLocale` only updates labels on existing editors at event time. If a user splits a group or opens a new window after changing locale, the new editor could be in the old language for built-in actions. The old reload avoided this because all modules re-evaluated. This is a real functional regression: **new editors created after a live switch do not get relocalized**, because `applyMonacoLocale` isn't called on editor creation. Unless `__calcpadTr` lazy resolution handles built-in action labels at editor creation: built-in `registerEditorAction` instances are created at module import, not per editor. `codeEditorWidget` uses `EditorExtensionsRegistry.getEditorActions()` which returns the global action instances; their `label` was resolved at import. So new editor copies the same old label. Since `applyMonacoLocale` mutated the global action instances' labels for supported actions on existing editors? It loops `editor.getSupportedActions()` and mutates each action object. Are those action objects the global registry instances or per-editor copies? In `codeEditorWidget.js:201-212`, it likely copies labels into `InternalEditorAction` per editor. Let's inspect. If `getSupportedActions` returns per-editor `InternalEditorAction` objects, mutating them only affects that editor. New editors get fresh copies from the global actions with old labels. This is a significant gap. Let's verify `codeEditorWidget.js` lines around 190-220 and `EditorExtensionsRegistry.getEditorActions`. Also `getSupportedActions` returns `this._actions`? Let's read.

Confirmed: per-editor InternalEditorAction copies from global `EditorExtensionsRegistry.getEditorActions()` at construction. `applyMonacoLocale` mutates per-editor actions, not global action labels. So new editors after a live switch get old-language labels for built-in actions, unless `applyMonacoLocale` is called again or Monaco uses lazy strings. This is a real regression relative to reload. But wait: for built-in actions, the global action label was resolved at module import; `applyMonacoLocale` could also mutate the global action registry, but it doesn't. It mutates `editor.getSupportedActions()` only. It also doesn't update `EditorExtensionsRegistry` action labels. So any editor created later (split, new window) will have old labels. This is significant and can be stated with evidence:
- `/.../codeEditorWidget.js:201-211` copies `action.label` from global registry at editor construction.
- `monaco-locale.ts:170-176` only iterates existing editors.
- `EditorExtensionsRegistry.getEditorActions()` global list not updated.
Thus new editor groups/windows after locale switch show previous language. Old reload re-evaluated modules; new window was a fresh webview and got current locale. In desktop multi-window, a new window created after switching locale loads the saved locale (per context) and is fine, but a new **split editor** in the same window after switch is stale. Also `applyMonacoLocale` doesn't get called on new editor creation. This is a concrete regression/gap.

Also `updateCalcpadActions` only updates existing editors and their actions; new editor's Calcpad actions are added via `addAction` with `translate` at creation, so those are okay. But built-in actions are stale. Context menu built-in labels for new editors are stale. The menu registry global titles were retranslated globally, so maybe context menu built-in items not from actions? Built-in context menu is generated from actions' labels, likely per-editor stale. Let's verify `contextmenu.js` uses `editor.getActions()` or contributions. It likely uses `this._editor.getSupportedActions()` to build menu; then new editor's actions stale. So yes.

Another gap: `applyMonacoLocale` does not update `EditorExtensionsRegistry` global actions, so even existing editors' newly constructed internal actions? They are already constructed. Fine.

Could the `MutationObserver` catch static strings in newly created widget? It translates DOM based on reverse map, so module-level static strings in newly opened find/suggest widgets **will** be translated by `translateText` because they are English text nodes matching reverse map. Ah! That's important: even if the module-level string is old-language English, the DOM observer translates it based on activeLocale. So new editors' find widget text would be translated by the observer. But built-in action labels in context menus are not necessarily DOM text? They are rendered into `.monaco-menu` and would be caught by `translateUi`/observer if the menu is inside selector. The menu DOM text is English; observer translates it. So new editor context menu labels may still get translated by the DOM walker. But action labels in command palette/quick input also DOM. Hmm. The DOM observer gives broad coverage for rendered text. However, it relies on reverse mapping exact English strings; dynamic text with shortcuts/keys may not match. Also `MONACO_UI_SELECTOR` only covers certain widgets. So not all.

Still, new editor action label mutation gap is less severe because DOM walker catches many rendered strings. But action labels used in non-DOM contexts (e.g. accessibility announcements, keybinding labels, aria attributes) may be stale. `translateAttributes` covers title/aria-label/placeholder on elements inside selector, but not all. We should present it as a gap/risk, not absolute breakage: new editors and widgets rely on DOM retranslation instead of the registry rewrite; surfaces outside the selector remain in the old language.

Let's check the `applyMonacoLocale` selector covers `.monaco-menu`, `.quick-input-widget`, `.find-widget`, `.suggest-widget .message`, dialog/rename boxes. It does not cover `.monaco-hover`, `.parameter-hints-widget`, `.peekview-widget`, `.notification-list-item`, `.breadcrumbs`, `.zone-widget`. So hover/parameter hints/peek/notifications are stale if already open, and new ones? New hover text is generated by lazy `__calcpadTr` calls after `__calcpadSetLocale` reset, so they should use new locale. But module-level static labels in hover maybe not. So mixed.

What about module-level `standaloneStrings` used for command palette placeholder/labels: DOM walker translates `.quick-input-widget` text nodes; likely covers. But dynamic phrases may not. Good enough to say "surfaces outside selector/dynamic strings can stay stale".

Now, another concrete regression: The old reload called `captureSession()` and `workspace.flush()` before reload. The new no-reload approach doesn't need those, but it also doesn't flush. If the app crashes or the user closes the window after switching locale, drafts autosave (10s debounce) still runs. No immediate loss. But there is a subtle issue: `captureSession` maybe was also needed for workspace; no longer. Not a regression.

Another concrete issue: The old listener was inside `if (isTauri && tauriBridge)`, meaning on web, locale switch left Monaco stale. The new listener outside fixes web too. This is an improvement. The current implementation's intent is to fix the P2 from prompt.txt. Good.

Another: The reload listener was registered only after `restoreSession`? In b26f2f7c it was placed before `restoreSession` function, inside Tauri block, after `captureSession` definition. It would be registered during bootstrap before session restore? Actually code order: listener added around line 2680, then `restoreSession` defined and called later. So reload could happen during bootstrap? No user interaction before mount? Fine.

Now, check `LOCALE_CHANGED_EVENT` event detail includes setting and locale. `applyMonacoLocale(getActiveLocale())`. Fine.

Now, native menu: `menuLabels(t)` filters untranslated. When switching back to English, labels = {}; Rust sets Some({}) and refreshes all windows → English. Fine. But because `MENU_LABELS` is global, window B's menu changes. As discussed.

Now, `menu.ts` change and 55b0154e: The user asks if 55b0154e updated Calcpad actions in MenuRegistry. We verified commandId format is correct (`editor.getId() + ':' + actionId`). But `updateCalcpadActions` uses `translate(messageId)` rather than `__calcpadTranslate(action.label, locale)`. Since activeI18n locale is updated before event, correct. It updates action labels and command titles. It also loops all menu items and sets `item.command.title = label` for matching commandId. Good. Potential issue: `editor.getAction(actionId)` returns the action stored under original id (`this._actions.set(id, internalAction)`), so correct. `registry._commands.get(commandId)` uses uniqueId; correct. Good.

Now, the `applyMonacoLocale` generic loop that rewrites all `_commands` and `_menuItems` can translate **user-defined** command titles? It only translates known strings; unknown remains. Fine. It may translate menu items' `item.title` for submenus, etc. Good.

Now, does `applyMonacoLocale` update **open context menu**? `translateUi()` selects `.monaco-menu`, so yes for text nodes. But context menu's items may be rendered as `aria-label` and text; covered. If the context menu is open when locale changes, the Vue setting panel is likely somewhere else; switching locale requires opening Settings (Vue sidebar), which may not close the Monaco context menu. The menu might be stale until reopened; not severe.

Now, production vs dev for Vite: The prebundle plugin `monacoPrebundle` is only in `optimizeDeps.rolldownOptions`. The production `plugins` array still `[monacoLanguagePacks(), vue()]`. So production unchanged. But `monacoTransform` was extracted in b07de4a2 from the inline transform; same logic. `monacoLanguagePacks` still has `enforce: 'pre'`; `monacoPrebundle` lacks `enforce: 'pre'`. In optimizer, plugin ordering might matter; if other plugins handle `.js`, but no other plugins in optimizer except internal. The transform must run before esbuild bundling; plugin transforms run before. Fine. Not production.

Potential dev risk: `optimizeDeps.rolldownOptions.plugins` is a Vite 8/rolldown option. The existing `build.rolldownOptions` indicates rolldown-vite. Fine. We can't verify runtime. We can state code inspection shows dev-only; no production build path reference. The `include: ['monaco-editor']` restores prebundling, and plugin applies transform during optimization. If the plugin fails to resolve the virtual module in the optimizer, dev may fail; but not production. Not a regression for users.

Now, the preview menu change: no production behavior difference except label composition. But one nuance: `shortcutLabel` uses `t(key)`; if a locale translates `common.copy` to a string containing placeholders? No. Fine. It appends `(Ctrl+C)` hardcoded, not localized shortcut names (Ctrl vs Cmd). Preexisting. On macOS, it shows Ctrl; preexisting. Not a regression.

Now, question 6: preserved, changed intent, unverified.

Preserved:
- The core reason for reload (Monaco labels/actions registered at startup) is acknowledged and addressed by in-place mutation of MenuRegistry, editor actions, DOM widgets; native menu already live; web now covered; tabs/unsaved work preserved (the explicit new intent).
- Locale persistence and next-window behavior: `writeLocaleSetting` runs before event; new windows/launches read it. This matches "next window reads saved locale".
- Server Accept-Language: `message-bridge/base.ts:153` sets locale provider to `getActiveLocale`; previews refreshed on event (`main.ts:2442`), so server-generated translated text updates. This preserves/improves the old intent from 5d7e0557/786535e1.
- Native menu sync preserved via watch (`main.ts:337-343`) and Rust global refresh (`lib.rs:638-640`).

Changed intent:
- Previously, reload was the accepted mechanism to guarantee full Monaco relocalization; now, live update is the intent (explicitly requested in the session transcript). The implementation intentionally accepts partial coverage. That's a change of strategy, not necessarily a bug.
- The old reload treated locale switch as a session-boundary event, flushing drafts/workspace. New implementation keeps session in memory; no flush. This is intended (keep tabs/unsaved work), but it removes the safety net; if a crash occurs before autosave, unsaved work could be lost (same as normal editing though).
- Cross-window: no broadcast existed; the new behavior (open windows keep language, next window reads saved) is consistent with prior behavior except that the old reload also only reloaded current window. So no intent broken. But native menu global update creates inconsistency across windows; if a broadcast was a new idea, its removal is not a regression from committed behavior.

Unverified:
- Did not run app/build; cannot confirm all Monaco surfaces update or that dev prebundle works.
- Cannot verify current behavior in an actual Tauri multi-window session (no runtime).
- No evidence of a committed locale broadcast; only found `broadcast` in agent-chat/doc-sync sync, and `BroadcastChannel` only in tab-drag (`tab-drag.ts:213`). The prior transcript explicitly said no locale broadcast was found. So the premise "broadcast removed" cannot be confirmed from git; it appears never to have existed in code.
- `9f2458e7` isn't an ancestor of HEAD; it's on backup branch `backup/i18n-unified-locale-20261122`. The current branch got the reload via `b26f2f7c`; 70cf4ed3 also not ancestor. This is important historical nuance. We should mention.

Wait, `70cf4ed3` not ancestor? The current branch's history includes `b26f2f7c`; maybe `70cf4ed3` is a cherry-pick on backup. The `git branch -a --contains 70cf4ed3` produced no output, meaning it's not reachable from any branch? Perhaps dangling. We can check `git log -1 --decorate 70cf4ed3` and `git branch --contains`. Now, deeper check for regression: `applyMonacoLocale` is called on locale change, but is it called at startup? No. At startup, `__calcpadTr` uses `__calcpadLocale()` which reads localStorage and window culture. If the persisted locale is `'auto'` and the desktop OS locale is non-English, `__calcpadLocale` sees localStorage `'auto'` (skips), then `window.__CALCPAD_CURRENT_CULTURE__` is NOT set on desktop (only VS Code provider injects it), then navigator language. Not caused by recent changes. But the live switch now uses `getActiveLocale()` (resolved) and `__calcpadSetLocale`, so after a change it's correct. The user says this is the intended new behavior ("janelas abertas mantêm o idioma, a próxima janela lê o locale salvo"). But the native menu is global and updates all windows, causing inconsistency. Is this a real regression? Before, changing locale in one window reloaded only that window; other windows' Vue/Monaco stayed old; native menu global changed. Same inconsistency. So not a regression; it's an existing limitation. The current task says broadcast was removed; if an implementation existed in a recent commit and was removed, maybe it was meant to fix this. But no code evidence. We can say: "If broadcast existed only as a plan, its removal leaves the pre-existing inconsistency; it does not conflict with a committed intent because none was committed."

Now, verify `window.location.reload` removal in `8f43e918` parent/current; blame lines in old block. We have commit diff. Good.

Now, the user asks "A troca ao vivo atual cobre essa intenção? O que ainda fica stale/quebrado em relação ao comportamento anterior?" We should answer:
- It covers the specific symptom that motivated reload: Calcpad action labels and most menus are updated in place; web is now covered too; tabs/unsaved preserved.
- It does not cover all Monaco internals. Concrete stale surfaces:
  1. Built-in action labels on **editors created after** the locale change: global `EditorExtensionsRegistry` labels aren't updated; per-editor copies from `codeEditorWidget.js:201-211` use old labels. `applyMonacoLocale` only mutates existing editors (`monaco-locale.ts:170-176`).   2. Monaco UI outside `MONACO_UI_SELECTOR` (hover, parameter hints, peek views, notifications, breadcrumbs, zone widgets, suggest item details) not retranslated in place; module-level strings among them stay old until reload. The selector is `monaco-locale.ts:62-70` and only those. (Some lazy strings will use new locale on next render because `__calcpadSetLocale` resets cache; but existing/open ones and module-level ones won't.)
  3. Dynamic text nodes (counts, "1 of 5", mixed strings) won't match the reverse map and remain old; `translateText` only translates exact core text (`monaco-locale.ts:76-88`).

Not a regression from previous reload, but the "broadcast removed" means no fix. If a new window is opened, it reads saved locale and is correct; existing windows are not synchronized.
  7. `refreshAllPreviews()` re-renders previews and resets scroll? It may cause preview flicker / scroll jump; old reload also lost preview scroll. Not necessarily a regression. But live switch now refreshes all previews, which can be expensive and may disrupt UI; `refreshAllPreviews` re-renders all groups. The old reload also rebuilt everything. Fine.
  8. `uiOverrideHints?.refresh()` and diagnostics/definitions refresh; okay.
  9. `set_menu_labels` global state: as above.
  10. No persistence of resolved locale for `auto` before event; `writeLocaleSetting(setting)` stores `'auto'`, not the resolved tag. On the next window, virtual module resolves Auto from OS/navigator. Fine. The context says next window reads saved locale; for Auto it reads setting and resolves. Fine.

**Base e veredito**

A intenção original era recarregar a webview porque o Monaco resolve o NLS e registra as ações uma única vez no startup. O reload era o mecanismo para garantir que **todo** o editor voltasse no idioma novo, aceitando perder/reconstruir estado. A intenção posterior — registrada no transcript do checkpoint `95d6c7a2` e no commit `8f43e918` — passou a ser explicitamente **não recarregar**, preservando abas e trabalho não salvo. A implementação atual cumpre essa segunda intenção em parte: cobre Vue, menu nativo, as quatro ações Calcpad e alguns widgets do Monaco, mas não é equivalente ao reload para todas as superfícies do Monaco e não sincroniza janelas.

Atenção histórica: `9f2458e7` e `70cf4ed3` **não são ancestrais de HEAD**. Eles estão na branch `backup/i18n-unified-locale-20261122`. O reload que existia nesta branch entrou por `b26f2f7c` e foi removido por `8f43e918`.

---

## 1. Que problema o reload original resolvia

Commit `9f2458e7` (“Reload the editor when the locale changes”):

> “Monaco resolves its NLS strings and the Calcpad editor actions are registered once, at startup. A live locale switch updated the Vue UI but left the editor menu in the previous language. Emit a locale-change event and let the desktop host flush drafts and the session before reloading the webview…”

O `70cf4ed3` dizia a mesma coisa: “The editor reloads when the UI locale changes so Monaco picks up the new language pack.”

O bloco removido em `8f43e918^` (`Calcpad.Web/frontend/calcpad-web/src/main.ts:2679-2700`) fazia:

```ts
captureSession();
for (const id of dirty) await writeDraft(id, true);
await workspace.flush();
...
window.location.reload();
```

Efeitos colaterais assumidos:

- **Drafts:** gravava todas as abas sujas antes do reload; o boot seguinte recuperava via `drafts-recovered`.
- **Sessão/workspace:** `captureSession()` + `workspace.flush()` persistiam apenas `openFiles`/`activeFile` (`workspace-state.ts:26-28`). Não preservavam split, ordem das abas, cursor, scroll, scroll do preview nem estado pendente do agente.
- **Menu nativo:** não dependia do reload. O `watch(localeRef, syncMenu)` já atualizava ao vivo (`main.ts:337-343`, blame `b26f2f7c`) e o Rust recompunha o menu de **todas** as janelas (`lib.rs:630-640`).
- **Outras janelas:** o reload era só da janela atual. O menu nativo delas mudava porque `MENU_LABELS` é global no Rust, mas Vue/Monaco continuavam no idioma antigo. O próprio transcript registra: “Não encontrei broadcast de locale para outras janelas”.
- **Web:** o listener ficava dentro de `if (isTauri && tauriBridge)`, então o build web não recarregava nem atualizava o Monaco. Isso era o P2 apontado no transcript.

O `b26f2f7c` melhorou a segurança do reload: `writeDraft(id, true)` e abortar o reload se a gravação falhasse (`8f43e918^` linhas 2690-2697). Essa rede de proteção desapareceu junto com o reload.

---

## 2. A troca ao vivo atual cobre essa intenção?

**Cobre:**

- Vue/i18n reativo (`i18n/index.ts:134-143`).
- Menu nativo ao vivo (`main.ts:337-343`; `lib.rs:638-640`).
- As quatro ações Calcpad via `55b0154e`: o `commandId` usado em `monaco-locale.ts:48` confere com o `uniqueId` gerado por `addAction` (`standaloneCodeEditor.js:118-120`).
- Títulos do `MenuRegistry` e menus de contexto existentes (`monaco-locale.ts:147-168`).
- Widgets no seletor `MONACO_UI_SELECTOR`: find, mensagem estática do suggest, quick input, menu, diálogos e rename (`monaco-locale.ts:62-70`), além do `MutationObserver` para nós novos (`113-139`).
- Preview, diagnostics e definitions são re-renderizados no evento (`main.ts:2438-2442`), e o `Accept-Language` do servidor usa `getActiveLocale` dinamicamente (`message-bridge/base.ts:153`).
- O listener agora vale também no build web (`main.ts:2433-2443`).

**Não cobre / fica stale em relação ao reload:**

- Superfícies fora do seletor: hover, parameter hints, peek view, notificações, breadcrumbs, zone widgets. O reload recriava tudo; agora só o que está no seletor é traduzido no DOM (`monaco-locale.ts:108-111`).
- Texto dinâmico ou composto (“1 of 5”, contagens, mensagens com números): `translateText` só traduz o texto exato e desiste se não houver correspondência única (`monaco-locale.ts:76-88`).
- Editores criados **depois** da troca: `codeEditorWidget.js:201-211` copia os labels das ações globais no momento da construção; `applyMonacoLocale` só percorre editores existentes no evento (`monaco-locale.ts:170-176`). O `MutationObserver` corrige muitos widgets visíveis, mas não o registro global nem superfícies fora do seletor.
- Traduções ambíguas: `__calcpadTranslate` devolve `undefined` quando o mesmo texto mapeia para IDs com traduções diferentes (`vite.config.ts:128-140`); nesses casos o label fica no idioma anterior.
- `retranslate` altera `value` **e** `original` (`monaco-locale.ts:21-29`), destruindo a fonte inglesa do objeto; voltar para um locale sem aquela chave pode manter a tradução anterior em vez de cair no inglês.
- Outras janelas: o evento é `window`-local; nenhuma janela aberta é atualizada.

Resumo: em relação ao **desktop antigo**, o sintoma principal (menu/ações no idioma velho) foi atacado, mas a cobertura é best-effort e não equivalente ao reload. Em relação ao **web antigo**, houve melhoria, porque antes não havia atualização nenhuma do Monaco.

---

## 1. Que problema o reload original resolvia

Commit `9f2458e7` (“Reload the editor when the locale changes”):

> “Monaco resolves its NLS strings and the Calcpad editor actions are registered once, at startup. A live locale switch updated the Vue UI but left the editor menu in the previous language. Emit a locale-change event and let the desktop host flush drafts and the session before reloading the webview…”

O `70cf4ed3` dizia a mesma coisa: “The editor reloads when the UI locale changes so Monaco picks up the new language pack.”

O bloco removido em `8f43e918^` (`Calcpad.Web/frontend/calcpad-web/src/main.ts:2679-2700`) fazia:

```ts
captureSession();
for (const id of dirty) await writeDraft(id, true);
await workspace.flush();
...
window.location.reload();
```

Efeitos colaterais assumidos:

- **Drafts:** gravava todas as abas sujas antes do reload; o boot seguinte recuperava via `drafts-recovered`.
- **Sessão/workspace:** `captureSession()` + `workspace.flush()` persistiam apenas `openFiles`/`activeFile` (`workspace-state.ts:26-28`). Não preservavam split, ordem das abas, cursor, scroll, scroll do preview nem estado pendente do agente.
- **Menu nativo:** não dependia do reload. O `watch(localeRef, syncMenu)` já atualizava ao vivo (`main.ts:337-343`, blame `b26f2f7c`) e o Rust recompunha o menu de **todas** as janelas (`lib.rs:630-640`).
- **Outras janelas:** o reload era só da janela atual. O menu nativo delas mudava porque `MENU_LABELS` é global no Rust, mas Vue/Monaco continuavam no idioma antigo. O próprio transcript registra: “Não encontrei broadcast de locale para outras janelas”.
- **Web:** o listener ficava dentro de `if (isTauri && tauriBridge)`, então o build web não recarregava nem atualizava o Monaco. Isso era o P2 apontado no transcript.

O `b26f2f7c` melhorou a segurança do reload: `writeDraft(id, true)` e abortar o reload se a gravação falhasse (`8f43e918^` linhas 2690-2697). Essa rede de proteção desapareceu junto com o reload.

**Mudou de intenção**

Ou seja, a troca de estratégia foi intencional.

- Sobre broadcast: não há implementação anterior commitada; a remoção não quebra uma intenção histórica, apenas deixa a inconsistência entre janelas que o reload também não resolvia.
